name: Abstract-Concrete Ratio
description: Analyzes the balance between abstract concepts and concrete language
mechanism: This method evaluates the proportion of abstract concepts versus concrete nouns in a text. LLMs often default to highly abstract, generalized language to avoid hallucinating specific details they lack context for. By cross-referencing words against psycholinguistic databases (like the MRC Psycholinguistic Database) for concreteness ratings, this method computes a weighted ratio. A disproportionately high reliance on abstract terms indicates potential AI generation, whereas human experts typically anchor abstract theories with concrete grounding.
parameters:
Analysis type: Psycholinguistic statistical
Media: Text
Input: Raw text string
Minimum text length: 150 words
Output: Abstractness ratio (0-100)
Processing: Lexical mapping & NLP correlation
accuracy: Moderate — 60-78% accuracy. Performance varies significantly by academic domain, as fields like philosophy or theoretical physics inherently feature high abstraction.
source: Psycholinguistics and NLP text abstraction analysis research.
useCase: Detection of default AI 'hedging and generalization' behavior. Most effective in distinguishing between authentic human expert writing (which uses specific concrete examples) and generalized AI essays.
strengths:
• Captures structural default behaviors of LLMs
• Grounded in established psycholinguistic concreteness metrics
• Highly effective on expository and argumentative essays
limitations:
• Heavily genre-dependent (poetry or philosophy skew the score)
• Requires a robust, language-specific dictionary of concreteness scores
• Can misclassify highly theoretical human academic works

references.title: Brysbaert, M., et al. (2014). Concreteness ratings for 40 thousand generally known English word lemmas. Behavior Research Methods.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
